title: Country sensitivity of domestic negative framing by media freedom

methods.eligibility: Identified government/action and numeric -1/0/+1 labels; zeros retained. Domestic country-month n >= 30.
methods.country_mean: Mean of that country's negative-framing shares over its eligible months. Pooled count share is separately labeled.
methods.group_mean: Each month's equal-country mean, then arithmetic mean across all 48 months. No smoothing in sensitivity summaries.
methods.monthly_weight: 1 / number of eligible countries in the fixed group in that month; zero contribution when ineligible.
methods.country_contribution: Mean across all 48 months of monthly country share times its monthly weight; reported in percentage points.
methods.leave_one_out: Remove one country from all months; recompute its group's equal-country means. Remaining memberships, threshold and months stay fixed; no regrouping.
methods.comparison: Low minus high group mean, in percentage points. Monthly rank counts use unsmoothed means and strict greater-than comparisons.
methods.share_units: Fractions from 0 to 1 unless the column ends in _pp; multiply fractions by 100 for percentages.

limits: A sensitivity diagnostic, not a preferred estimator or a reason to discard a country.
These counts cannot identify which outlets, genres, events or coding decisions explain a country's rate.
Equal-country weighting answers a different question from pooling all articles. Within country-months, included articles remain pooled across sources.
Fixed media-freedom groups are descriptive; no causal effect or population-representative country coverage is established.
